**Hint 1**
For problems where we need to construct something under some conditions, then a good idea is to first see the nature of the sequences that satisfy the conditions.

**Hint 2**
The given condition is that $$$a_{\text{gcd}(i, j)} \neq \text{gcd}(a_i, a_j)$$$ all $$$i \lt j$$$. As the given operation is gcd on indices and values, it's hard to directly find the properties of the sequence.

**Hint 3**
One way to check the sufficiency is to find a contradiction.

**Hint 4**
Imagine two indices $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ where $$$i$$$ does not divide $$$j$$$ but the condition is violated: $$$a_{\text{gcd}(i, j)} = \text{gcd}(a_i, a_j)$$$. Then $$$g = \text{gcd}(i, j)$$$ is a divisor of both $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ and as $$$a_g$$$ divides both $$$a_i$$$ and $$$a_j$$$, so for pair $$$(g, i)$$$ we have $$$a_{\text{gcd}(g, i)} = a_g$$$ and $$$\text{gcd}(a_g, a_i) = a_g$$$ because $$$a_g$$$ divides $$$a_i$$$. So for this pair the condition is violated! So if the condition is violated for some pair $$$(i, j)$$$ then it is violated for the pair $$$(g, i)$$$ and $$$(g, j)$$$ as well where $$$g = \text{gcd}(i, j)$$$.

**Hint 5**
So if there is no pair $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ where $$$i$$$ divides $$$j$$$ and the condition is violated, then all the pairs also satisfy the condition. This proves the sufficiency of the condition.

**Hint 6**
So we have found a necessary and sufficient condition. Now we need to construct the lexicographically largest sequence that satisfies the condition.

**Hint 7**
Consider a multiple chain $$$i_1 \lt i_2 \lt \ldots \lt i_k$$$ such that $$$i_1$$$ divides $$$i_2$$$, $$$i_2$$$ divides $$$i_3$$$, ..., $$$i_{k-1}$$$ divides $$$i_k$$$. Then we know that we have to put distinct values for all the indices in the multiple chain otherwise one number will be divisible by another which will violate the condition.
